<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `sysc-greet-mango.install` script performs standard post-install, post-upgrade, and pre-removal operations typical of an AUR package for a graphical greeter. It creates a dedicated `greeter` user with appropriate system groups (`video`, `render`, `input`) for hardware access, sets up required directories under `/var/lib/greeter` and `/var/cache/sysc-greet`, and configures file ownership and permissions accordingly. The script backs up the existing `greetd` configuration before replacing it with a new one that launches the `mango` greeter as the `greeter` user.

During upgrades, it ensures the `greeter` user remains correctly configured and updates directory permissions. On removal, it disables the `greetd.service`. All operations are confined to expected system paths and service management. The use of `systemctl`, `useradd`, `usermod`, `chown`, and `mkdir` is consistent with legitimate system integration tasks. Output messages, including version notes and ASCII art, are informational and pose no risk.

No suspicious network activity, code execution, or data exfiltration is present. The script does not download or evaluate remote content, nor does it manipulate files outside its intended scope. While it overwrites `/etc/greetd/config.toml`, this is expected behavior for a greeter package configuring its display manager backend.
</details>
